# Founding Fuel: Learning & Education — Batch 1 (2015–2019) — Dense Observations

---

## RECURRING ARGUMENTS FF MAKES ON THIS THEME

**1. Lifelong learning as existential necessity, not aspiration**
"To stay relevant, I have to learn all the time" (KV Kamath) is presented as the foundational premise. This argument recurs constantly across authors.
— SOURCE: "The Learned Life" by Charles Assisi (2015-03-16)

FF frames the urgency in competitive/evolutionary terms: "Else, I fear rapid change will make me obsolete" and "the next dog is going to have me for its next meal."
— SOURCE: "How to be insanely more productive" by Charles Assisi (2016-08-02)

**2. Learning is inherently messy, not linear**
"Learning is ugly" — drawn from Ramsey Musallam, and echoed in Kamath's 1997 Internet-era observations: young hackers who "just got into the game" and "figured things out as they went."
— SOURCE: "The Learned Life" by Charles Assisi (2015-03-16)

**3. Curiosity before answers; questions over answers**
"All discovery, all invention, all innovation are outcomes of curiosity, of inquisitiveness, of asking all manner of questions." FF repeatedly privileges question-asking over answer-giving: "We are taught to answer, rather than question; we are taught to equate knowledge with knowing answers."
— SOURCE: "Why questions score over answers" by Founding Fuel (2015-06-26)

**4. Deliberate practice, not mere repetition, builds expertise**
The Ericsson "deliberate practice" framework is invoked multiple times across different authors (Assisi, Chakraborty, Shivakumar). FF is consistent: unconscious competence from automation is the enemy of true expertise.
— SOURCE: "Work Smart. Not Hard" by Kavi Arasu (2015-08-18)
— SOURCE: "Only perfect practice makes perfect" by Indranil Chakraborty (2016-12-27)
— SOURCE: "The Beatles, and mastery through deliberate practice" by Founding Fuel (2018-12-30)

**5. Training programmes as broken, ritualistic, and largely ineffective**
"Is training an anachronism that the business world continues to cling to?" The sausage-factory critique of corporate L&D is sharp: executives dragged in, no link to business outcomes, treated as entitlement (leadership programmes at US vs. Indian b-schools), and unable to demonstrate impact.
— SOURCE: "The end of training" by Founding Fuel (2015-11-17)

**6. Learning embedded in work, not separated from it**
Asian Paints' model (disbanding the annual training calendar, six focused programmes linked to business outcomes), K Ramkumar's credit-learning apprenticeship story, and Maira's call for "learning to learn" all converge: "Work is the learning and learning that is embedded in work sticks."
— SOURCE: "The end of training" by Founding Fuel (2015-11-17)
— SOURCE: "Learning to stay relevant" by Founding Fuel (2019-07-14)
— SOURCE: "Diwali cleaning for the mind" by Founding Fuel (2019-10-13)

**7. Management/b-school education is misaligned with India's actual needs**
India needs execution-focused, implementation-oriented MBAs, not pale imitations of American programmes. "India's biggest management challenges lie in execution and getting things done in a complex environment."
— SOURCE: "How to create an Indian MBA" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-03-26)

**8. The gap between academia and practice as a systemic failure**
Research in b-schools is written by academics for academics. Practice is leading theory, not the reverse. "By common consensus, research isn't advancing practice or the science of management in any great degree."
— SOURCE: "Bridging the gap between academia and practice" by Indrajit Gupta (2017-12-16)
— SOURCE: "How business schools in India have killed off research" by Harsh Vardhan (2018-01-14)

**9. Liberal arts and interdisciplinary thinking as undervalued**
From multiple angles — Tanuj Bhojwani's IIT critique, Scott Hartley's podcast, Krishnan's management guru analysis — FF argues that STEM alone is insufficient. "The value of technology is in solving meaningful human problems."
— SOURCE: "What they don't teach you at the IITs" by Tanuj Bhojwani (2019-10-05)
— SOURCE: "Where do ideas come from?" by Founding Fuel (2019-10-20)

**10. Ethics cannot be adequately taught in a classroom alone**
"Can one teach ethics in a class, or is ethics a way of thinking and being, that is imbibed from family and social norms?" — posed repeatedly in the MasterClass series as an unresolved tension.
— SOURCE: "Creating Ethical Leaders: Will management education rethink its role?" by Ajit Rangnekar (2019-09-27)
— SOURCE: "Creating Ethical Leaders: Can ethics be taught?" by R Gopalakrishnan (2019-09-30)

---

## FF'S INDIA-SPECIFIC ANGLE

**India as a vast laboratory of wasted human potential**
"One of the biggest tragedies of India has been the waste of human potential." VidyaGyan is celebrated precisely because it finds the best and brightest from families earning under Rs 1 lakh/year — talent that would otherwise never surface.
— SOURCE: "VidyaGyan: Allowing Indian Talent to Flower and Bloom" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-03-16)

**India's b-schools: Global in quantity, poor in quality**
India accounts for a quarter of all global b-schools but only three have AACSB accreditation. "These numbers are inflated by India alone accounting for a quarter of all global business schools."
— SOURCE: "How to create an Indian MBA" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-03-26)

**The peculiar Kerala paradox: literate but unemployable**
The doctoral dissertation ghost-writing economy in Kerala chayakadas is a vivid India-specific diagnosis: mass literacy without employable skill or intellectual independence. "Highly literate, unemployed bloke."
— SOURCE: "Doctoral dissertations from a tea stall" by Charles Assisi (2015-05-24)

**India's unique management context: family businesses, diversity, government**
Indian MBAs need specific capabilities: managing without Western-style structures, managing government stakeholders, managing a culturally diverse and aspirational workforce.
— SOURCE: "How to create an Indian MBA" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-03-26)

**Brain drain of management talent**
"Why do [Indian management academics] have to emigrate to achieve that status?" CK Prahalad, Sumantra Ghoshal, Jagdish Sheth — celebrated abroad, couldn't have risen in India.
— SOURCE: "What does it take to become a Management Guru?" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2015-04-06)

**India as diabetes capital, and other "grand challenges"**
India-specific scale problems (50 million Type II diabetes patients, 200 million children in government schools) require India-specific innovation, not transplanted Western models.
— SOURCE: "How to innovate for India" by Indrajit Gupta (2017-12-30)
— SOURCE: "Change is possible for public education in India. Azim Premji shows how" by Founding Fuel (2017-11-01)

**Swayam/MOOCs as India's access opportunity**
India "lacks enough good high-quality higher education institutions" and "doesn't have enough trained faculty." Technology-based learning is not a luxury but a necessity at the country's scale.
— SOURCE: "Will India's tryst with online courses pay off?" by Indrajit Gupta (2016-09-28)

**SSISM (Sandalpur) as the counter-model**
A privately-built, idealistic college in rural MP — 14 girl students winning university ranks, graduates in Cognizant, Infosys, SAP — presented as proof that "idealistic, innovative entrepreneurship" can transform higher education at the grassroots.
— SOURCE: "Idealistic, innovative entrepreneurship has the potential to change Indian higher education" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2016-01-04)

**Indian millennial workforce management as distinct challenge**
Indian millennials require a more nuanced reading than Western stereotypes. Kalpathi's book is praised for grounding analysis in Indian organisations (HCL, InMobi, Ola) rather than generalising from Western data.
— SOURCE: "Understanding India's millennials" by Rishikesha T Krishnan (2017-01-17)

---

## FRAMEWORKS, THINKERS, AND MENTAL MODELS

**Deliberate Practice (Anders Ericsson)**
Most frequently invoked learning framework across the batch. Appears in at least four separate articles. Consistently contrasted with mere repetition/unconscious competence.
— SOURCE: "Work Smart. Not Hard" by Kavi Arasu (2015-08-18); "Only perfect practice makes perfect" by Indranil Chakraborty (2016-12-27); "The Beatles, and mastery through deliberate practice" by Founding Fuel (2018-12-30)

**Four Stages of Competence (Noel Burch / Gordon Training International)**
Unconscious incompetence → conscious incompetence → conscious competence → unconscious competence. Used to argue that automation = enemy of expertise.
— SOURCE: "Work Smart. Not Hard" by Kavi Arasu (2015-08-18)

**Hedgehog vs Fox (Isaiah Berlin / Tetlock)**
Tetlock's superforecasting research valorises the fox over the hedgehog. "Be a fox." Used as a model for good thinking and forecasting.
— SOURCE: "Six people who can help you become a superforecaster" by NS Ramnath (2015-10-28)

**Fermi-izing (Enrico Fermi)**
Breaking complex questions into estimable sub-questions. Used as a model for intellectual courage and working under uncertainty.
— SOURCE: "Six people who can help you become a superforecaster" by NS Ramnath (2015-10-28)

**5 Whys (Sakichi Toyoda / Toyota)**
For root-cause analysis in questioning discipline.
— SOURCE: "Why questions score over answers" by Founding Fuel (2015-06-26)

**Gigerenzer's Heuristics / Ecological Rationality**
The distinction between risk (knowable probabilities) and uncertainty (unknowable). In uncertainty, simple rules of thumb outperform complex models. "An adaptive toolbox."
— SOURCE: "Gigerenzer's simple rules" by NS Ramnath (2017-02-19)

**VUCA / IVI World (Arun Maira)**
Maira's "IVI (Innovation-VUCA-Innovation)" framing extends the standard VUCA framework to argue that management education faces a "double bind."
— SOURCE: "Learning to learn" by Arun Maira (2018-04-19)

**Systems Thinking (recurring Maira framework)**
Systems thinking is presented as a foundational discipline that must be taught. Contrasted with piecemeal, check-box approaches.
— SOURCE: "Learning to learn" by Arun Maira (2018-04-19); "Diwali cleaning for the mind" by Founding Fuel (2019-10-13)

**Effectuation vs. Causal Reasoning (Saras Sarasvathy)**
Entrepreneurial learning follows effectuation — working with available means, remaining open — not pre-determined causal logic.
— SOURCE: "How entrepreneurs learn" by Indrajit Gupta (2019-04-20)

**Kahneman's System 1 / System 2 (Thinking Fast and Slow)**
Referenced as a framework for understanding cognitive biases and decision quality.
— SOURCE: "11 things to explore, learn and reflect on in 2020" by R Sriram (2019-12-24)

**Question Formulation Technique (Rothstein & Santana / Right Question Institute)**
Formal pedagogy for teaching question-asking. Cited with approval as a structured method.
— SOURCE: "Why questions score over answers" by Founding Fuel (2015-06-26)

**Benjamin Franklin's writing practice**
Cited twice as the canonical example of deliberate practice applied to a cognitive/creative skill.
— SOURCE: "Only perfect practice makes perfect" by Indranil Chakraborty (2016-12-27); "The Beatles, and mastery through deliberate practice" by Founding Fuel (2018-12-30)

**Conscious Leadership / Above/Below the Line (Dethmer)**
"Above the line: open, curious, committed to learning. Below the line: closed, defensive, committed to being right."
— SOURCE: "11 things to explore, learn and reflect on in 2020" by R Sriram (2019-12-24)

**Chunk and Compound (mental models)**
FF's own internally-named framework for accelerating learning: break material into manageable units (chunk), combine perspectives (compound).
— SOURCE: "Chunk and compound to learn more, and learn fast" by Founding Fuel (2019-05-04)

**Parkinson's Law**
"Work expands so as to fill the time available." Used in the productivity/learning context.
— SOURCE: "How to be insanely more productive" by Charles Assisi (2016-08-02)

---

## WHAT FF IS SKEPTICAL OF / PUSHES BACK AGAINST

**Psychometric tools as selection filters**
Kamath's experiment: 50 validated leaders, only one would have been selected by standard psychometric tools. "Most of the HR functionaries responsible for talent acquisition…have not taken the time to sit back and reflect on the limitations." Sharp critique of lazy, ill-informed practice.
— SOURCE: "Putting psychometrics in perspective" by K Ramkumar (2016-12-17)

**IQ tests and "whiz kids" paradigm**
"The high IQ 'whiz kids' in John F Kennedy's administration crafted 'brilliant policies that defied common sense' with respect to Cuba and Vietnam." IQ ≠ leadership capacity.
— SOURCE: "Putting psychometrics in perspective" by K Ramkumar (2016-12-17)

**Big Data as a panacea**
"More data alone cannot help to make sense of what is happening in the world." Gigerenzer's work is explicitly deployed against the faith in complex algorithms and optimisation.
— SOURCE: "Gigerenzer's simple rules" by NS Ramnath (2017-02-19); "Learning to learn" by Arun Maira (2018-04-19)

**TED Talk culture as shallow performance**
The Tai Lopez critique is biting: "How do you read a book a day? Sometimes I take a week. But sometimes, books only have one or two things that are worth reading." FF identifies "performance monkeys on the TED stage" — articulate people giving audiences false permission to learn superficially.
— SOURCE: "Performance monkeys on the TED stage" by Charles Assisi (2017-10-14)

**10,000-hour rule (Gladwell's version)**
Gladwell's formulation is corrected: Ericsson, the original researcher, said quality matters — practice must be deliberate and purposeful, not merely accumulated.
— SOURCE: "The Beatles, and mastery through deliberate practice" by Founding Fuel (2018-12-30)

**B-school campus placements as a game of "hit and miss"**
"Nearly 70% of students quit their first job after graduating within nine months to a year." The 100% placement record is a vanity metric. Business schools, HR departments, and media rankings are all complicit.
— SOURCE: "The b-school campus placement BS—and how to clean it up" by Indrajit Gupta (2018-01-27)

**"One Big Story" reductionism in learning and leadership**
"The real world is often about juggling two contradictory principles, it's about trade-offs, it's about finding a balance." Focused-mode vs. diffuse-mode learning (Barbara Oakley) is deployed against single-minded prescriptions.
— SOURCE: "The real world vs the idea of One Big Story" by Founding Fuel (2019

# Founding Fuel: Learning & Education — Batch 2 (2020-01-05 to 2020-11-23)

## RAW OBSERVATIONS WITH SOURCES

---

### RECURRING ARGUMENTS FF MAKES ON LEARNING & EDUCATION

**Learning requires discomfort and active resistance to cliché**
- The editor's resolution to "make myself comfortable with discomfort" by entering a church sets the theme for the year: genuine learning requires engaging with what one has already written off. — SOURCE: "On being comfortable with discomfort" by Founding Fuel (2020-01-05)

- "At a time when there is an information overload, it's easy to jump from an essay here to a podcast there, spreading ourselves too thin. It's far better to focus on a few quality learning materials, and dig deeper." — SOURCE: "Why we should re-examine the clichés in our heads" by Founding Fuel (2020-02-17)

- The Polish dancer's story: the city producing bad dancers had "delicious" lessons with "tons of new information" but no excellence. The city producing great dancers focused on one core thing per lesson, drilled to perfection. "The takeaway from her narrative is depth matters over breadth." — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #167: FF Recommends science movies to binge watch" by Founding Fuel (2020-09-05)

**Learning requires slowness, reflection, and space**
- "We fantasize about being Neo in The Matrix and learning a new trick by just downloading materials straight to our brains. But learning happens best when we give ourselves enough space to think, reflect—and even sleep over it." — SOURCE: "Why we should re-examine the clichés in our heads" by Founding Fuel (2020-02-17)

- Barbara Oakley: "Your brain needs breaks. The effects of too much focusing time might be even further magnified when society promotes relaxation mechanisms, such as certain forms of meditation, that also encourage focus." Both focused and diffuse (open-monitoring) modes are needed. — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #146: FF Recommends | Note Taking Apps" by Founding Fuel (2020-08-16)

**Learning-how-to-learn is the meta-skill**
- Haresh Chawla at IIM Bangalore breakout: "One of the sessions I take with MBA students is learning how to learn. They really are not very clear as to why and what they need to pick out of the MBA programme. Every rule of business you know used to get upturned every 20 years; now it gets upturned every five years. They have to learn to be curious. They have to learn to create mental models of the world." — SOURCE: "Working From Home Daily #99: First principles thinking" by Founding Fuel (2020-06-30)

**Reading is a core discipline, not casual consumption**
- Ram Charan: "Investing a half hour a day in reading, seven days a week, 365 days a year, is a habit that will bring more value to you and your leadership strength than any other investment of your time." Charlie Munger: "You have to have a temperament to grab ideas and do sensible things." — SOURCE: "Working From Home Daily #82: Grab new ideas, make reading a habit" by Founding Fuel (2020-06-13)

- Charles Assisi: "While writing is difficult, reading the right way is tougher. A good writer can write nonsense in pretty words. But it takes an intelligent reader to interrogate a book, the writer, and the thinking, to go past the obvious and form an independent opinion." — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #118: How to find good books" by Founding Fuel (2020-07-19)

**Direct experience is irreplaceable but has limits**
- Peter Senge: "The most powerful learning comes from direct experience…But what happens when we can no longer observe the consequences of our actions?…We each have a 'learning horizon'." — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #95: Learn from direct experience" by Founding Fuel (2020-06-26)

**Curiosity is an engine, not an ornament**
- Ian Leslie: Paul Harris estimates children ask 40,000 "explanatory" questions between ages 2-5. "These explanatory questions can be profound or silly... Questioning is an incredibly important engine for cognitive development." "Stay curious." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #209: Stay curious" by Founding Fuel (2020-10-20)

- Ian Leslie on "diversive curiosity" vs "epistemic curiosity": the former is where the hunt begins; the latter is "what happens when diversive curiosity grows up"—the deepening into directed understanding. — SOURCE: "FF Daily #236: The hunt for knowledge" by Founding Fuel (2020-11-23)

**Tacit knowledge is systematically undervalued**
- Russell Ackoff story: trained engineers fail to measure furnace temperature; illiterate old worker does it by timing his spittle evaporation, taught by his predecessor. "Ackoff's bigger point is not about the wisdom that comes from working on a shop floor, but an organisation's willingness and ability to tap that knowledge. Often leaders look at one space for solutions, thereby precluding some of the most creative and effective solutions." — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #156: The ability to tap tacit knowledge" by Founding Fuel (2020-08-26)

**Mentorship requires tough love and honest feedback**
- Robert Greene: "Masters are those who by nature have suffered to get to where they are…As mentors, they alone can gauge the extent of our progress, the weaknesses in our character, the ordeals we must go through to advance. In this day and age, you must get the sharpest dose of reality that is possible from your mentor." — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #170: To achieve mastery you need tough love" by Founding Fuel (2020-09-09)

---

### FF'S INDIA-SPECIFIC ANGLE

**Digital education's prerequisites missing in India**
- Sonajharia Minz, VC of Sido Kanhu Murmu University in Jharkhand: "Till date, some districts in Odisha have no roads and electricity. If digital education becomes the final medium of teaching in the post-lockdown phase, we will be consciously depriving and eliminating a section which does not have access to this platform." And: "think of the family with one phone and four children." — SOURCE: "Working From Home Daily #1 - 70" by Founding Fuel (2020-06-01)

- Bloomberg report on poor students falling through cracks; Shantha Sinha of Mamidipudi Venkatarangaiya Foundation: "Instead of innovating, governments and schools have gone for the easiest option available... It's showing a lack of sensitivity." FF frames this as a structural failure with bottom-up solutions needed. — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #126: Humans affect change, but tech shows the possibilities" by Founding Fuel (2020-07-27)

**Indian MBA is excessively Westernized and needs rebalancing**
- Ajit Rangnekar: "Global companies wanted people who understood their way of working, and also understood India realities…we focused too much on that. We need to readjust now. And it is happening already. Since 2006 or thereabouts, the focus has shifted back to India. The methodology is global, but how you apply is far more local with more Indian case studies." — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #122: Practise physical, not social, distancing" by Founding Fuel (2020-07-23)

**Indian B-schools have neglected research**
- FF curates Harsh Vardhan's essay "How business schools in India have killed off research" as essential pre-reading for its MBA Masterclass, signaling this is a systemic Indian institutional failure, not just a curriculum issue. — SOURCE: "Working From Home Daily #99: First principles thinking" by Founding Fuel (2020-06-30)

**India's New Education Policy (NEP) assessed on its own terms**
- Meeta Sengupta: "The New Education policy leads with three radical changes that will bring much needed relief from the pipeline approach that had trammelled much of our students' potential. First is the excellent initiative of allowing students in HE to collect credits and step away from HE and return when they can (within limits). Life happens to us all—it should not be a reason to lose an entire year." — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #130: What the New Education Policy gets right" by Founding Fuel (2020-07-31)

**Aadhaar as a design case study in "less is more"**
- "When the designers of Aadhaar were deciding on the demographic details to collect, they kept it to the minimum because it will be more inclusive, less prone to mistakes and easier to scale." Used as evidence for the "less is more" principle in learning design. — SOURCE: "Why we should re-examine the clichés in our heads" by Founding Fuel (2020-02-17)

**India's technology policy on frontier science**
- Amrita Chowdhury: "India is one of the few countries which has an AI policy at the government level and there is a huge amount of funding and institution building that is being thought of and spoken about… And India just announced the budget for quantum." Framed as hopeful but requiring more institutional depth. — SOURCE: "Building a career in frontier science" by Founding Fuel (2020-09-01)

**IIT Madras as model of research-to-commercialization**
- Prof. Ashok Jhunjhunwala and the TeNet Group cited as rare Indian example of academic research spawning real startups (corDECT WLL, Banyan Networks, n-Logue), with a parallel to Reliance Jio. — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #192: Exercise is a creative act" by Founding Fuel (2020-10-02)

**Gender disparity in employment worsened by pandemic**
- Mahesh Vyas (CMIE): Women held only 11% of 403 million total jobs in 2019-20. Of 11 million lost jobs in August 2020, 4 million were women's jobs (disproportionate to their share). "Women lost jobs in demonetisation, they lost jobs because of GST, and again we see women lose jobs disproportionately compared to men in this shock as well." — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #176: The art of speaking effectively" by Founding Fuel (2020-09-15)

**Privacy education framed as Indian public health problem**
- Justice Srikrishna: "Many think it's fine if the government takes their data, without realising that privacy is their fundamental right. Unfortunately, people don't understand the value of this right. They are also right because India has bigger problems—food, water, shelter and jobs. Therefore, it's important that it should be a part of their DNA, and we need to massively educate people." Parallel drawn to RBI educating on banking, SEBI on markets. — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #128: The genius inside you" by Founding Fuel (2020-07-29)

---

### FRAMEWORKS, THINKERS, AND MENTAL MODELS

**Clayton Christensen — "Jobs to be done"**
- Cited as "one of the finest thinkers and teachers of our times," wielding "as much influence as the head of a state." His death triggers a full tribute issue. His 25-year framework on innovation and the personal-professional integration of his work explicitly held up as a model for how learning should work. — SOURCE: "The life and times of Clayton Christensen" by Founding Fuel (2020-01-29)

**Peter Senge — The Fifth Discipline / Learning Organization**
- Cited twice: on direct experience and learning horizons; and on how failure should be seen as "evidence of the gap between vision and current reality" not unworthiness. The learning organization as the organizational ideal. — SOURCES: "WFH Daily #95: Learn from direct experience" (2020-06-26); "WFH Daily #118: How to find good books" (2020-07-19)

**Nassim Taleb — Antifragility and tinkering**
- Antifragile as a cliché-buster: "some things benefit from shocks; they thrive and grow when exposed to volatility." Also: "the strategy for the discoverers and entrepreneurs is to rely less on top-down planning and focus on maximum tinkering." — SOURCES: "Why we should re-examine the clichés in our heads" (2020-02-17); "WFH Daily #169: Nassim Taleb on tinkering" (2020-09-08)

**Carol Dweck — Growth Mindset**
- Jaime Escalante teaching inner-city Hispanic students college-level calculus: "'With the right mindset and the right teaching, people are capable of a lot more than we think.'" "He asked, 'How can I teach them?' not 'Can I teach them?'" — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #122: Practise physical, not social, distancing" by Founding Fuel (2020-07-23)

**Robert Greene — Mastery**
- Used to argue that tough feedback from mentors is not optional but essential: "Get them to give you the proper challenges that will reveal your strengths and weaknesses." Mastery requires "toughness and a constant connection to reality." — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #170: To achieve mastery you need tough love" by Founding Fuel (2020-09-09)

**Arun Maira — Systems thinking**
- "A new Enlightenment founded on 'systems thinking' is required to understand complexity—not by breaking complexity into simpler components, but by understanding patterns and relationships among the components of complex systems. Children are taught to think of the world in compartmentalized subjects…knowledge of systems as a whole is falling apart." — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #107: Study the system, not its fragments" by Founding Fuel (2020-07-08)

**Srikant Datar — "Knowing, Doing, Being" gap**
- "MBA programmes' focus has been on 'knowing', not so much on 'being' or 'doing'." Framed as the central failure of management education globally. — SOURCE: "Masterclass: The Future of the MBA" by Founding Fuel (2020-07-22)

**Peter Kaufman — Three Buckets / Multidisciplinary Thinking**
- Long extract from Kaufman's 2018 talk: three sample buckets (13.7 billion years of inorganic universe; 3.5 billion years of biology; 20,000 years of human history) as the basis for models that "no one else in the world uses." Ludwig Wittgenstein: "To understand is to know what to do." — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #175: A multidisciplinary approach to thinking" by Founding Fuel (2020-09-14)

**John Gardner — Personal Renewal**
- 1990 McKinsey speech: the barnacle metaphor for people who "run out of steam in midcareer." "There's a myth that learning is for young people…It's what you learn after you know it all that counts." "Learn all your life. Learn from your failures." — SOURCE: "WFH Daily #124: Personal renewal; stayin' alive; and the constants of technology" by Founding Fuel (2020-07-25)

**Daniel Goleman — Emotional Intelligence**
- Samurai/Zen master story used to illustrate: "The sudden awakening of the samurai to his own agitated state illustrates the crucial difference between being caught up in a feeling and becoming aware that you are being swept away by it." Awareness = the keystone of emotional intelligence. — SOURCE: "Working From Home Daily #90: A laptop for working and one for studying" by Founding Fuel (2020-06-21)

**Anthony de Mello — "Tying the cat"**
- Story of guru's cat tied during worship, continued for centuries, with learned treatises written to justify it. "The key insight of the story is not just that some systems and processes continue even when there is no reason for them to, but it's that over time we come up with new reasons. That's where we have to apply the 'first principles thinking'." — SOURCE: "Working From Home Daily #99: First principles thinking" by Founding Fuel (2020-06-30)

**Rolf Dobelli — Hindsight Bias / Ovarian Lottery**
- Hindsight bias: "makes us believe we are better predictors than we actually are, causing us to be arrogant about our knowledge." Antidote: journaling. Ovarian lottery (Buffett via Dobelli): what you are you owe to your genes and environment — gratitude and redistribution are the only rational responses. — SOURCES: "WFH Daily #204: The hindsight bias" (2020-10-14); "WFH Daily #168: The ovarian

# Learning & Education — BATCH 3: Dense Observations

## REPEATED ARGUMENTS ACROSS ARTICLES

**Reading and learning as foundational practices**
"At Founding Fuel there are two things we place a premium on—reading and learning. This hypothesis has stood scrutiny over the years each of us on the team have had with some of the finest minds across the world." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #256: How to generate ideas" by Founding Fuel (2020-12-16)

Reading demands active engagement, not passive consumption: "you must tackle books that are beyond you, or, as we have said, books that are over your head. Only books of that sort will make you stretch your mind." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #407: Pick a book that challenges you" by Founding Fuel (2021-06-29)

**Note-taking and knowledge management as learning infrastructure**
"I try to offload knowledge as soon as possible into my notes—making sure to restate, in my own words, the concepts contained in the book or the article so that not only do I understand it better, I can re-frame it in the context of my current state of knowledge on the subject." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #257: How to 'remember' everything" by Founding Fuel (2020-12-17)

**Self-knowledge about learning style as prerequisite for performance**

Adam Grant/Alison Wood Brooks: labelling fear as "excitement" rather than "calm" produced 17% more persuasive speeches, 15% more confidence, 29% longer speeches, 22% better math scores. "Fear is an intense emotion... trying to relax is like slamming on the brakes when a car is going 80 miles per hour." — SOURCE: "FF Insights #689: Excited versus calm" by Founding Fuel (2022-10-07)

**Practical experience in employment before entrepreneurship**
"Most first-time entrepreneurs then set up ventures in the industries where they had been working. Research is also consistent in showing that entrepreneurs who set up ventures in industries where they have previously worked have a higher likelihood of survival and success." — SOURCE: "From employee to entrepreneur" by S. Ramakrishna Velamuri (2023-07-22)

**Philosophy as lived practice, not academic exercise**
Indian traditions' approach of shravana (listening), manana (contemplating), nidhidhyasana (applying in practice) as a model for engaging with philosophical ideas. — SOURCE: "FF Life: Engaging with philosophy" by N S Ramnath (2023-07-28)

**Visual thinking as undervalued cognitive skill**
"Doodling sharpens your visual thinking and communication skills, which are important for today's world." Conscious doodling is described as meditative and as a tool for "connected art." — SOURCE: "FF Life: Notes from a rookie doodler—five lessons" by N S Ramnath (2022-09-20)

**Slow reading as resistance to speed culture**
Carl Honore's "cult of speed" critique applied to learning: "One of the sad outcomes of this is that we seem to be losing the art of slow reading." Passage Meditation proposed as systematic antidote. — SOURCE: "FF Life: The art of slowing down" by N S Ramnath (2024-01-27)

**The education system mistakes the measure for the goal**
"The goal of education was always to teach thinking—knowledge was simply a measure of that thinking. Somewhere along the way, we confused the measure with the goal. Instead of focusing on fostering deep thought, we turned education into a test of memory." — SOURCE: "AI in Academia: The Grind, the Gain, and the Great Recalibration" by Kavi Arasu (2025-02-11)

**Reading remains essential for leadership relevance**
"If you don't read you'll become irrelevant very fast. Read as much as you can. That's the only way you can ensure a long and relevant career." — SOURCE: "23 Takeaways from Founding Fuel Live: The Best Business Books of Summer 2024" by Founding Fuel (2024-07-02)

## INDIA-SPECIFIC ANGLE

**India's linguistic diversity as both gift and problem for knowledge access**
"Our linguistic diversity is a gift but keeps a treasure chest of Indian knowledge locked." Bhashini project under National Language Translation Mission described as "a global first" model of collaborative AI. 1,200 languages in India require translation infrastructure before learning can be democratized. — SOURCE: "FF Insights 710: Why writing matters" by Founding Fuel (2022-11-14)

**India's education system as production line, hierarchy-bound**
Students in Indian classrooms see education as a "production line." The teacher-as-sole-authority model is "quietly being challenged" by AI. "If I ask a question in class, the teacher might say it's not in the syllabus. Why wait a year when ChatGPT gives me the answer in seconds?" Indian classroom hierarchy: "teachers are the source of all answers." — SOURCE: "AI in Schools: Not a Generational Divide, but a Dialogue Waiting to Happen" by Ipsita Bandyopadhyay, Ishani Ray (2025-05-23)

**International school conundrum: expensive, elite, but genuinely different**
IB and Cambridge IGCSE schools "remain on the fringes"—only ~600 IGCSE schools and ~210 IB schools across India. The "prevailing obsession with grades" contrasts with international boards' encouragement of innovation in "teaching and learning, assessments, professional development." — SOURCE: "FF Life: The international school conundrum" by Ambica Naithani (2023-09-08)

**Indian academic culture equates rigour with range, causing cognitive overload**
"Much of our academic culture in India equates rigour with range—with cramming every possible topic into a course. The unintended consequence is cognitive overload: students under pressure, resorting to memorisation rather than building the habits of critical thinking." — SOURCE: "Relearning the Craft of Teaching" by Uma Narain (2026-01-30)

**Chess as case study in ecosystem-building and inspiration cascades**
Manuel Aaron → Viswanathan Anand → 26 Tamil Nadu grandmasters. "When Anand became the first Indian Grandmaster, it inspired a whole generation of Chennai players." Each World Championship triggered a new cohort. Model of mentorship, institution-building, and inspiration cascades. — SOURCE: "FF Insights #706: Chennai's chess pioneers" by Founding Fuel (2022-11-14)

**Entrepreneurship pendulum may have swung too far in India**
"At the turn of the century, entrepreneurship in India was not considered an attractive occupation... Today, I am worried that the pendulum may have swung too far in the opposite direction." Shark Tank India cited as contributing to making regular employment "decidedly uncool." — SOURCE: "From employee to entrepreneur" by S. Ramakrishna Velamuri (2023-07-22)

**AI adoption in India: employees learning AI on personal data before work data**
"Employees today are using AI on themselves before they use AI at work... With no other technology has this happened. We didn't learn Excel on our own before we went to a company Excel sheet." — SOURCE: "Founding Fuel Live | The Best Business Books of 2024" by Founding Fuel (2024-12-13)

**India's 22 scheduled languages and 780+ indigenous tongues at risk from AI monoculture**
"India — with 22 scheduled languages, over 780 indigenous tongues, and hundreds more spoken in markets, songs, and stories — is home to dozens at risk." Karya (Kannada datasets) and Vidhai Project (Tamil) cited as early efforts. — SOURCE: "The Love of One's Tongue in the Age of AI" by Kavi Arasu (2025-08-13)

**Constitutional literacy as civic learning**
We The People Abhiyan facilitates workshops "mostly in rural India, mostly with people from marginalised communities" on constitutional rights and responsibilities. Stories from the Constitution's making used as pedagogy. — SOURCE: "We, the People of India" by Vinita Gursahani Singh (2025-01-31)

## FRAMEWORKS, THINKERS, MENTAL MODELS

**Recurring frameworks:**

- **Neuroplasticity as learning model**: Brain rewires based on repeated engagement. Tinkering activates "sensory feedback, motor control, spatial reasoning, prediction, error correction, and delayed gratification." — SOURCE: "When We Stopped Taking Things Apart" by Ajay Chacko (2026-01-11)

- **Evergreen Notes (Andy Matuschak)**: Atomic, concept-oriented, heavily interlinked written notes as antidote to information hoarding. — SOURCE: "FF Life: Collect & Connect — managing information overload" by N S Ramnath (2023-03-18)

- **Passage Meditation (Eknath Easwaran)**: Memorize inspirational passages, recite slowly, don't follow associations, 30 minutes daily. Framed as systematic antidote to speed culture. — SOURCE: "FF Life: The art of slowing down" by N S Ramnath (2024-01-27)

- **Shravana-manana-nidhidhyasana**: Indian philosophical framework for engaged learning: listen, contemplate, apply. — SOURCE: "FF Life: Engaging with philosophy" by N S Ramnath (2023-07-28)

- **The Tail End (Tim Urban)**: Week-chart framework for visualizing remaining life, focusing attention on what matters. — SOURCE: "Wabi Sabi, life is long, and other reflections" by R Sriram (2023-01-02)

- **Viktor Frankl's Will to Meaning**: "Between stimulus and response, there is a space." Contrasted with Freud's will to pleasure and Adler's will to power. — SOURCE: "Wabi Sabi, life is long, and other reflections" by R Sriram (2023-01-02)

- **Inglehart-Welzel Cultural Map**: Used to show every major LLM clusters in "Protestant Europe/English-speaking quadrant"—"they can speak 35 languages, but they think in one." — SOURCE: "The Love of One's Tongue in the Age of AI" by Kavi Arasu (2025-08-13)

- **Inside Out Leadership (McKinsey Bower Forum)**: Leaders need "a much deeper sense of their own purpose. Who are they? What is their identity?" Peer coaching among CEOs as substitute for feedback that no longer reaches the top. — SOURCE: "Founding Fuel Live | The Best Business Books of 2024" by Founding Fuel (2024-12-13)

- **Successism (Chip Conley)**: "A cultural condition where identity and worth are shaped by inherited definitions of success." Midlife as moment of rupture with inherited success scripts. — SOURCE: "Embracing Life's Second Arc" by Founding Fuel (2026-02-13)

**Recurring thinkers:**

## WHAT FF IS SKEPTICAL OF / PUSHES BACK AGAINST

**Against the mythology of leadership**
K Ramkumar: "Leadership is triggered or demanded by a certain context. Otherwise it's a myth. We hold leaders in a mythological way—their characteristics are always noble." Jeffrey Pfeffer's *Leadership BS* recommended explicitly for "exploding leadership myths." — SOURCE: "FF Life: Best leadership books—7 essential reads" by Founding Fuel (2022-10-15)

**Against purpose-washing in corporations**
D. Shivakumar: "I think 90% of CEOs don't know what they're talking about" on purpose. Hari: "The idea of purpose has suddenly become very important because people are stuck in boring jobs. When that happens, you need to look for fulfillment outside of your work." — SOURCE: "Do leadership books matter?" by Founding Fuel (2022-12-12)

**Against the quantification paradigm in personal development**
Triathlete Siddharth Shetty: "The data from the smartwatch was influencing my training... But now I know that was absolute bullshit!" Coach's lesson: a student who "used to measure everything... never won a single medal." — SOURCE: "FF Life: What I've learnt from training to be a triathlete" by Founding Fuel (2022-09-10)

**Against AI sentience claims**
"In case you are wondering if it has become sentient, we would say, 'no way'." Citing Timnit Gebru and Gary Marcus. — SOURCE: "FF Insights #678: Teaching yourself" by Founding Fuel (2022-08-30)

**Against blanket AI restriction in academia**
The California Faculty Association resolution described as "quite the contrary" to what FF would advocate. The real challenge: "not what AI should do—it's what humans should still do." — SOURCE: "AI in Academia: The Grind, the Gain, and the Great Recalibration" by Kavi Arasu (2025-02-11)

**Against the "efficiency kills learning" assumption**
"It is easy to assume that efficiency threatens deep learning. The grind—rewriting a paper, wrestling with ideas, receiving tough feedback—h[as value]" — the article pushes back against *both* naive AI adoption and naive AI restriction. — SOURCE: "AI in Academia: The Grind, the Gain, and the Great Recalibration" by Kavi Arasu (2025-02-11)

**Against social media "humility display"**
David Brooks: "you must always use the word humbled when the word proud would actually be more accurate." Cited with evident approval of Brooks' critique. — SOURCE: "FF Insights #690: How we interpret information" by Founding Fuel (2022-10-07)

**Against PowerPoint-centered teaching**
"Glued to the screen, it became easy to teach through the deck rather than to the students. Eye contact thinned. Rapport weakened." — SOURCE: "Relearning the Craft of Teaching" by Uma Narain (2026-01-30)

**Against covering everything as a definition of academic rigour**
"At Bok, rigour did not come from covering everything. It came from slowing down, choosing a few foundational ideas, and returning to them until understanding deepened." — SOURCE: "Relearning the Craft of Teaching" by Uma Narain (2026-01-30)

**Against the digital-only learning paradigm**
"Most of the products and services we rely on — especially digital ones — are no longer designed to be understood, only to be used." The maker mindset vs. supervisory mindset distinction. — SOURCE: "When We Stopped Taking Things Apart" by Ajay Chacko (2026-01-11)
